title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #6

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What are the two main types of things carried by the stem? (1 mark)
   A. Sound and light
   B. Heat and cold
   C. Water and food
   D. Air and stones

2. Which of these is a safety rule when handling plants? (1 mark)
   A. Ask an adult before touching a plant you do not know
   B. Taste every fruit you find
   C. Rub sap on your eyes
   D. Pull plants with thorns barehanded

3. Which sign of life is shown when a yellow leaf falls from a tree? (1 mark)
   A. Making fruit
   B. Removing waste
   C. Breathing in
   D. Reproducing

4. Ostrich and flamingo belong to which group? (1 mark)
   A. Amphibians
   B. Birds
   C. Mammals
   D. Reptiles

5. How many legs does an insect have? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Ten
   C. Four
   D. Eight

6. What does the large intestine do with the leftovers? (1 mark)
   A. Turns them into saliva
   B. Chews them
   C. Takes back water and forms faeces
   D. Swallows them

7. What is vomiting? (1 mark)
   A. Feeling hungry
   B. Chewing food
   C. Food coming out through the mouth
   D. Passing loose faeces

8. Which of these is true of a solid? (1 mark)
   A. It keeps its shape wherever it is put
   B. It has no mass
   C. It takes the shape of any container
   D. It cannot be measured

9. Sand pours like a liquid. What state is each grain? (1 mark)
   A. Steam
   B. Gas
   C. Liquid
   D. Solid

10. Which of these is a liquid used as fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Paraffin
   B. Firewood
   C. Air
   D. Charcoal

11. A cup can hold about (1 mark)
   A. 2500 ml
   B. 25 litres
   C. 25 ml
   D. 250 ml

12. Why is it good to separate waste into different bins? (1 mark)
   A. It makes reusing, recycling and composting easier
   B. It makes waste heavier
   C. It makes waste smell
   D. It makes waste burn

13. Why are gumboots useful when handling waste? (1 mark)
   A. They make waste lighter
   B. They make hands clean
   C. They protect the feet from sharp things and dirt
   D. They make waste rot

14. Which of these is a source of fresh water? (1 mark)
   A. A puddle of sea water
   B. The sea
   C. A river
   D. A salty lake only

15. A tap leaks 3 litres each hour. How much is wasted in one day of 24 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 24 litres
   B. 48 litres
   C. 27 litres
   D. 72 litres

16. Who should practise water conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Only farmers
   B. Only teachers
   C. Everyone at home and school
   D. Only adults

17. Which of these is true of water? (1 mark)
   A. Animals do not need water
   B. Water is needed by all living things
   C. Only humans need water
   D. Plants do not need water

18. A tap leaks 2 litres every hour. How much is wasted in 5 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 7 litres
   B. 2 litres
   C. 10 litres
   D. 25 litres

19. What does drip irrigation do? (1 mark)
   A. Cleans the soil
   B. Makes rain
   C. Floods the whole field
   D. Gives water to each plant a drop at a time

20. Which surface gives the most friction? (1 mark)
   A. A smooth ice surface
   B. A polished tile
   C. An oiled floor
   D. A rough carpet

21. What does a force do when it squeezes a sponge? (1 mark)
   A. Changes its colour
   B. Makes it hot
   C. Makes it lighter
   D. Changes its shape

22. Which surface gives the least friction? (1 mark)
   A. A wet, oiled tile
   B. Dry grass
   C. Rough sandpaper
   D. A thick carpet

23. Which force pulls objects down towards the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. Gravity
   B. Wind
   C. Friction
   D. Sound

24. Which small living thing makes its own light and so is a natural source? (1 mark)
   A. Firefly
   B. Electric bulb
   C. Torch
   D. Candle

25. Which battery-powered device gives artificial light? (1 mark)
   A. Firefly
   B. Sun
   C. Torch
   D. Stars

26. You want to see if a material is opaque. What do you do? (1 mark)
   A. Taste it
   B. Weigh it
   C. Smell it
   D. Shine a torch at it and see if light passes

27. Which of these is the biggest natural source of light for the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. The sun
   B. A candle
   C. A star far away
   D. The moon

28. Which of these passes heat slowly? (1 mark)
   A. Aluminium
   B. Iron
   C. Wood
   D. Copper

29. At what temperature does water boil? (1 mark)
   A. 50 degrees Celsius
   B. 100 degrees Celsius
   C. 0 degrees Celsius
   D. 10 degrees Celsius

30. What is evaporation? (1 mark)
   A. Water freezing
   B. Water being poured
   C. Water becoming a solid
   D. Liquid water turning into a gas

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain why a spider is not an insect. (3 marks)

32. Explain why the flat paper and stone dropped together do not land at the same time. (3 marks)

33. Describe three examples each of reducing and reusing water. (4 marks)

34. Sort into decomposable and non-decomposable: egg shells, tin can, cotton cloth, polythene bag, cow dung, glass bottle. (4 marks)

35. Give two ways in which water is wasted at school. (2 marks)

36. Convert 4 kg into grams. (2 marks)

37. Describe the methods of conserving water. Include reducing, reusing and recycling with examples. (5 marks)

38. Explain how wasting water can affect other people and the family. (4 marks)

39. Give four healthy eating habits that keep the digestive system healthy. (4 marks)

40. Describe the characteristics that show that animals are living things. Use examples. (5 marks)

41. Describe how animals respond to changes around them. Give four examples. (4 marks)

42. Give two examples each of vertebrates and invertebrates, and state one feature of each group. (4 marks)

43. Describe how a wheelbarrow makes work easier and how it is looked after. (4 marks)

44. State the difference between mass and volume. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Water and food
   The stem carries water and mineral salts up and food made in leaves to other parts.

2. A — Ask an adult before touching a plant you do not know
   Some plants can hurt or poison people, so ask first.

3. B — Removing waste
   Old leaves may carry waste away when they fall.

4. B — Birds
   Both have feathers and lay eggs.

5. A — Six
   All adult insects have six legs.

6. C — Takes back water and forms faeces
   Water is absorbed and the rest becomes solid waste.

7. C — Food coming out through the mouth
   Vomiting is throwing up food through the mouth.

8. A — It keeps its shape wherever it is put
   A solid has a definite shape.

9. D — Solid
   Each grain is a small solid.

10. A — Paraffin
   Paraffin and petrol are liquid fuels.

11. D — 250 ml
   A cup holds about 250 ml.

12. A — It makes reusing, recycling and composting easier
   Sorting helps each type be managed properly.

13. C — They protect the feet from sharp things and dirt
   Boots protect feet from cuts and germs.

14. C — A river
   Rivers carry fresh water that people can use.

15. D — 72 litres
   3 x 24 = 72 litres.

16. C — Everyone at home and school
   Everyone shares water and should save it.

17. B — Water is needed by all living things
   All living things need water.

18. C — 10 litres
   2 x 5 = 10 litres.

19. D — Gives water to each plant a drop at a time
   It gives water slowly at the roots.

20. D — A rough carpet
   Rough surfaces give more friction.

21. D — Changes its shape
   Squeezing changes the shape.

22. A — A wet, oiled tile
   Oil and smoothness reduce friction.

23. A — Gravity
   Gravity pulls things towards the centre of the Earth.

24. A — Firefly
   Fireflies make their own light.

25. C — Torch
   A torch is made by people.

26. D — Shine a torch at it and see if light passes
   If no light passes, it is opaque.

27. A — The sun
   The sun lights the Earth in the daytime.

28. C — Wood
   Wood is a poor passer of heat.

29. B — 100 degrees Celsius
   Pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

30. D — Liquid water turning into a gas
   Evaporation changes a liquid into a gas.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Insects have six legs and three body parts. A spider has eight legs, so it is not an insect. It is an invertebrate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for six legs, 1 mark for eight legs, 1 mark for conclusion.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gravity pulls both down but air pushes up on the flat paper more, so it falls slowly. The stone is little affected by the air.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for gravity on both, 1 mark for air pushing paper, 1 mark for stone landing first.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Reduce: close taps, fix leaks, use a cup. Reuse: washing vegetables water on plants, laundry water for mopping, rainwater for the garden.
   Working / marking points: Award marks for correct examples up to a total of 4.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decomposable: egg shells, cotton cloth, cow dung. Non-decomposable: tin can, polythene bag, glass bottle.
   Working / marking points: Award 4 marks for all correct, 3 for five, 2 for four and 1 for three.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Leaving taps running, leaking taps or pipes, using too much water for washing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: 4000 g.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 x 1000 and 1 mark for the answer with units.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: Reduce wastage: close taps. Reuse: washing vegetables water on plants. Recycle: cleaning used water at a treatment plant or filtering. Include rainwater harvesting.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three methods, 1 mark for correct examples and 1 mark for harvesting.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Less water is left for others, especially in dry areas. The family pays more for water and may have to fetch more.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for others and 2 marks for family.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Eat a balanced diet, eat fruits and vegetables, drink clean water, chew slowly, wash fruits, avoid rotten food, cover food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each habit up to 4.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: Animals feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond and die. Give examples such as a goat eating grass and a hen laying eggs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign to a maximum of 5.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: A goat lifts its head at noise, a snail pulls into its shell when touched, birds fly away from danger, animals seek shade in hot weather.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each of three examples.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Vertebrates: goat and tilapia, have a backbone. Invertebrates: ant and snail, have no backbone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two vertebrates, 1 mark for feature, 1 mark for two invertebrates, 1 mark for feature.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: The wheel rolls so friction with the ground is small. It is easier to push than drag a load. Oil the joints and wheel axle to reduce friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for wheel, 1 mark for less friction, 1 mark for oil, 1 mark for care.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and volume is the space it takes up.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct meaning.
